title: Permeability Units: H/m, µ_r and Why Iron is 1000× Air
h1: Magnetic permeability units — H/m and relative permeability
description: µ₀ = 4π × 10⁻⁷ H/m. Relative permeability µ_r is dimensionless. Iron alloys hit µ_r = 5000+; mu-metal 100 000+.

author.name: The Turbo Unit Converter engineering desk

reviewer.name: Turbo Unit Converter editorial review
reviewer.credential: verified against NIST SP 811 and category-specific ISO references

hero: µ = µ₀ × µ_r links B and H: B = µH. Confuse µ with µ_r and you overshoot core sizing by three orders of magnitude.
body: Permeability tells you how effectively a material carries magnetic flux for a given driving field. It is the slope of the B–H curve in the linear region. Two versions coexist: the absolute permeability (H/m) and the dimensionless relative permeability µ_r.

> µ₀ = 4π × 10⁻⁷ H/m ≈ 1.2566 × 10⁻⁶ H/m (permeability of free space)
> µ_r = µ / µ₀ (dimensionless)
> B = µ H = µ_r µ₀ H
Air, vacuum, most non-magnetics: µ_r ≈ 1. Aluminium: µ_r ≈ 1.000022. Silicon steel (transformers): µ_r = 4000–10 000. Mu-metal: µ_r up to 100 000. Superconductors (perfect diamagnet): µ_r = 0.

A mu-metal enclosure with µ_r = 80 000 reduces ambient 50 µT (earth field) by roughly µ_r inside a closed shell — down to <1 nT. Same enclosure in aluminium (µ_r ≈ 1) does nothing. Get the unit right or the shielding budget disappears.
µ_r is a ratio; µ has units of H/m. Multiply µ_r by µ₀ to get absolute permeability.

faqs.a: No — real materials saturate. µ_r drops sharply as B approaches the saturation value (~2 T for silicon steel).
At high frequencies µ becomes complex — the imaginary part accounts for hysteresis and eddy-current loss.
